projects.name: Personal website
projects.whatIsThis: A one-page portfolio with a live GitHub contributions heatmap and a résumé that prints from the page itself.
projects.whyThisChoice: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript on GitHub Pages: one page needs no framework or build step, and it deploys on every push.
projects.whatBreaks: If the GitHub contributions API is unreachable, the activity card drops the GitHub view and falls back to a map of the visitor's own visit; the social preview image needs an absolute URL once the site has a domain.
projects.whatILearned: A recruiter decides in seconds, so the proof (roles, logos, numbers) has to sit above the fold; extra sections mostly add scroll.

projects.name: Flash Report AI
projects.whatIsThis: A retrieval-augmented app that turns corporate documents (PDF, DOCX, CSV) into cited executive reports, exported as styled DOCX.
projects.whyThisChoice: Retrieval with maximal marginal relevance, so a report draws on several different passages instead of near-duplicates of one.
projects.whatBreaks: Answers are only as good as retrieval: a question whose answer is spread across documents can come back incomplete. It needs an OpenAI key to run.
projects.whatILearned: Executives trusted the reports once every claim cited its source passage; without citations a correct report still got second-guessed.
metrics: Retrieval tuning over 10,000+ chunks cut token cost about 60%

projects.name: Stone Scraper
projects.whatIsThis: Scrapes a web page, cleans the HTML, and lets you ask a local language model to pull structured data out of it.
projects.whyThisChoice: Local models through Ollama, so page content stays on the machine and parsing costs nothing per call.
projects.whatBreaks: Selenium scraping breaks when a site changes its layout or blocks automated browsers; the parse step needs a local Ollama model running.
projects.whatILearned: Getting clean HTML out of real sites broke far more often than the model's parsing did; most of the work is in the scraper, not the LLM.

projects.name: moodle-mcp
projects.whatIsThis: An MCP server (about 950 lines of Python) that lets Claude read a student's Moodle: what's due, course files, announcements and grades.
projects.whyThisChoice: It signs in with the personal token Moodle gives its phone app and calls the app's own web-service API, so it sees exactly what the app sees, without scraping or asking for a password.
projects.whatBreaks: It only works on Moodle sites that allow the mobile app, and stops when the token is revoked or expires.
projects.whatILearned: About 950 lines of Python turned Claude into something I use daily for school; a narrow tool with the right data beats a general assistant.

projects.name: Diagram check (CPSC 415 team project)
projects.role: Team of two with a classmate. Ralston built the server, model calls, validator, page and eval (tests first) and wrote the spec; the classmate approved the plan and reviewed the pull requests.
projects.whatIsThis: A web app that draws a labeled science diagram for a chosen topic, then has a vision model check the picture itself against a hand-written checklist; the grade is computed in code.
projects.whyThisChoice: The critic never sees the generation prompt, so it has to judge the image, and the model never grades itself: our code turns its observations into the verdict.
projects.whatBreaks: The critic misses labels that point at the wrong part: it passed a circuit whose 'wire' label points at the battery.
projects.whatILearned: GPT-4o graded a circuit with a wrong label 'good' every time. Only an eval set with planted flaws caught it, so I don't trust a vision model's judgment until I've tested it.

projects.name: Receipt reader with an arithmetic check (CPSC 415 lab)
projects.whatIsThis: A command-line tool that reads a receipt photo into JSON with a vision model, then checks in plain code that the items, tax and total add up.
projects.whyThisChoice: The model reads; integer-cent arithmetic decides. Two models were compared on the same receipts before picking the cheaper one.
projects.whatBreaks: Names and dates are not arithmetic, so a misread store name gets through; real photos cost five times the tokens of clean scans.
projects.whatILearned: The model read $9.99 as $6.99 but got the total right; only the arithmetic check in plain code caught it. Let the model read and let code decide.

projects.name: Skill-improvement loop (at Ramp)
projects.evidenceNote: Employer work: the only public evidence is his own site. Keep details at the level the site states.
projects.whatIsThis: Mines agent failures from Langfuse traces and proposes prompt changes that a person approves before they ship.
projects.whyThisChoice: Every proposed prompt change is checked against past failures before a person approves it.
projects.whatBreaks: A fix can pass the old failures and still regress cases nobody logged.
projects.whatILearned: Most agent failures were the same few patterns repeating; mining traces found them faster than reading complaints.

projects.name: Field SMS agent (at Datagrid)
projects.evidenceNote: Employer work: the only public evidence is his own site.
projects.whatIsThis: Construction crews text a question and get an answer from their project's data.
projects.whyThisChoice: Crews already text, so SMS needed no app install or training.
projects.whatBreaks: Answers are only as current as the project data behind them, and SMS can't show drawings or long documents.
projects.whatILearned: Crews on site would never open a new app, but they already text; putting the agent in SMS is what got it used.
metrics: Adoption directly supported a six-figure enterprise deal; used on $200M+ construction projects

projects.name: Roblox game with his brother
projects.evidenceNote: In development, not shipped. The chatbot must not describe it as a released game.
projects.whatIsThis: A game in development, built in Roblox Studio and Blender with AI agents driving both through their MCP servers.
projects.whyThisChoice: Agents drive Roblox Studio and Blender through their MCP servers, so two people can build a game's worth of content.
projects.whatBreaks: An agent can edit the wrong object or ship an untested change, so every change needs a check in Studio.
projects.whatILearned: Driving Roblox Studio and Blender through MCP, the agent is only as good as what it can see; screenshots and checks after every change matter more than the prompt.
